survivors.label: equivalent_or_optional
survivors.reason: Removing the explicit equal-p-value tie shortcut preserves Benjamini-Hochberg values on normalized Fisher p-values. In the reverse sorted scan, for a tie p_i=p_(i+1), last_bh is at most p_i*m/(i+2), hence no greater than p_i*m/(i+1). The mutant min(last_bh, p_i*m/(i+1)) therefore returns last_bh just like the shortcut; induction covers longer ties. Non-ties use the same minimum in both versions. This uses the downstream sorted/reverse/min consumer logic, not merely that the mutant differs from the reference. The stored multiple-trait/tied-p consumers pass.
